correctness_confidence.basis: The proofs of Theorems 2.1, 3.1, and 4.1 are mathematically sound: the 169-product closure, rank counts (16, 96, 57), idempotents, Green's J/H-classes, Harary matching-parity argument over the 16 forest cases, T_6/T_8 witnesses, and matrix powers for C_3, C_6, K_4 and Remark 4.2 all check out.

rigor.basis: Section 5 establishes an explicit three-layer verification boundary separating universal Lean 4.36.0 proofs (T01-T20, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) from 16 zero-float Bareiss certificates (C01-C16) and cited results from [2, 5, 6], with clear proofs and legible Figures 1-3.

novelty.basis: Building on [5, 6], the paper resolves the open Section 6 extension from paths to arbitrary trees (Theorem 3.1), uncovers the contrast between the 11/13 single-path deficit and 13/13 single-tree surjectivity, and establishes exact linear and exponential cycle-escape formulas (Theorem 4.1).

significance.basis: The results establish the exact spectral dichotomy separating universal forest determinant collapse (|det| <= 1 in Theorem 3.1) from unbounded cyclic escape (Theorem 4.1) and correct a numerical slip in [6, Example 5.1], completing the tree-closure theory for 1-joined graphs.

reproducibility.basis: Section 5 provides exact SHA-256 digests for the Lean source, zero-float Bareiss Python verifier, and certificate manifest alongside 16 certificates (C01-C16), 61 pytest checks, 20 zero-sorry Lean 4.36.0 theorems, and an exhaustive 1,441-tree Prufer audit (C09).

summary: This paper resolves the open tree-extension problem of Pinzon et al. (Section 6) by proving that all finite labeled forests collapse into the 13-element monoid M_13 while single labeled trees surject onto all 13 elements via witnesses T_6 and T_8. It characterizes M_13's 169-product Cayley table and Green's eggbox structure, proves exact cycle-escape determinant laws for C_3, C_6, and K_4, and audits Section 5 chain examples while flagging a path-count erratum (4050 vs. 5050). Claims are rigorously partitioned across 20 Lean 4.36.0 proofs, 16 zero-float Bareiss certificates, and cited literature.
strengths: Theorem 3.1 gives an elementary, airtight proof via Harary's expansion [2] that every labeled forest collapses into M_13, paired with explicit minimal witnesses T_6 and T_8 achieving full 13/13 surjectivity unlike single paths.

Theorem 4.1 pins down the exact boundary of finiteness by deriving closed-form determinants k+1, (-4)^k, and (-1)^k(2k+1) for iterated 1-joins of C_3, C_6, and K_4, matching Figure 2 and Remark 4.2's independent chain audits.

Section 5 establishes an exemplary three-layer verification boundary distinguishing universal Lean 4.36.0 matrix proofs (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) from finite Bareiss certificates and cited graph-theoretic lemmas.
weaknesses: In Theorem 2.1(4), the universal 11/13 single-path exclusion of {+-E_22} for arbitrary path lengths n > 8 is cited from [6] and checked up to n <= 8 in C01 rather than given its short parity-matching proof in Section 2 or listed explicitly in Layer 3 of Section 5.

The graph-to-matrix bridge (Harary's matching uniqueness on forests [2] and the 1-join identity [5, 6]) is imported from literature rather than formalized over graph types inside Lean, so formal verification of universal collapse covers the 16 parity-matrix cases in T13.
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal Tree Collapse and Single-Tree Surjectivity (Theorem 3.1): proves via Harary matching parity that every finite labeled forest maps into M_13 while witnesses T_6 and T_8 hit +-E_22 to reach all 13 elements.

Exact Cycle- and Clique-Escape Laws (Theorem 4.1): establishes sharp closed-form linear, exponential, and alternating linear determinant growth formulas k+1, (-4)^k, and (-1)^k(2k+1) for iterated 1-joins of C_3, C_6, and K_4.
